annotations.text:
E · PRESS — CHOSEN (#138).
C's grid and C's faces, B's material, and the part of D that worked (the block below Common Grounds). Cream ground; ink appears ONCE, as a contained band.

GROUND is the locked #f2eee2 from #136 — a cooled variant was tried and reverted. A real background TEXTURE is wanted for the final and is not decided here.

GRIT: a tiled print grain (placeholder, deliberately strong), concrete at the masthead, halftone at 13–14px pitch, hatching in the ink band. Portraits warmed with sepia rather than flat grey.

ORDER: theme, then latest news, then the 2026 archive, then the archive cards. That order is load-bearing — no 2027 artists exist yet, so news carries the page today and the 2026 grid is labelled as archive.

STILL OPEN: the final texture, and whether the reduced-leg mark at 375px holds.

A · INDEX — riskiest.
The mark is the only large element; the site becomes a numbered parts catalogue of what already exists. Every number is real (111 / 66 / 5 / 125 / 29).

WHY: most faithful to the MSCHF register in the map's Notes — deadpan, institutional, humour in the rigour. Costs nothing to author and never goes stale: the counts update themselves from Supabase.

TRADEOFF: a visitor who wants a festival poster gets a directory instead. Row 003 shows the pipe crossing type with a knockout — the one place the motif appears at page scale.

B · STATEMENT — ink poster.
One screen: mark, year on its dimension leader, one line, one action. The archive is a strip, not the body.

WHY: highest impact per pixel, and the only direction that reads as a poster rather than a website. The concrete blocks and the downcomer do the work the content isn't doing.

TRADEOFF: it says almost nothing. If someone arrives wanting the lineup or the schedule, they are one strip away from bouncing. Also the least to look at on a return visit.

C · ARCHIVE — cream, portraits as the body.
28 of the 111 portraits shown, greyscaled so the red still reads as the only colour. The pipe runs in the GUTTER between grid rows — the one place on a photographic page where the knockout ground still exists (#137).

WHY: zero new authoring, and the most human page of the four. Faces sell a festival.

TRADEOFF: the whole page is last year. Without a strong 2027 line at the top it can read as an archive site rather than a live one. Greyscale is a real decision to accept or reject.

D · OPENER — keeps the 2026 image.
The safest end, but not conventional: the photo is framed by pipe rails and the mark sits on a SOLID INK SLAB dropped over the image, because the knockout halo cannot survive a photographic ground.

WHY: least disruptive to what exists, and the image is genuinely good.

TRADEOFF: the slab is the compromise — judge whether it reads as deliberate or as a logo in a box. The photo also does most of the talking, so the new identity does the least work here.
